::: {.scope}
[What "certified" means here]{.lbl}
A **verified first-order saddle** on that model's own potential-energy surface, for this
reconstructed cluster with an inferred charge and spin, whose ±imaginary-mode relaxations
reach valid reactant-like and product-like minima. It says **nothing about accuracy against
DFT**, and the ±mode check is **not an IRC**.
:::

What the comparison shows, and what it does not:

- **Both models describe the same hydride-transfer saddle.** Each has exactly one imaginary
  mode dominated by the transferring H, the same Sn–O set at the saddle, and the two saddle
  geometries differ by 0.40 Å over the whole cluster (0.095 Å for the reactive core). Starting
  the OMOL saddle search from Tian's POLAR saddle gives the identical OMOL saddle.
- **OMOL puts the barrier 40.6 / 35.6 kJ/mol lower** than POLAR, depending on which reference
  state is used, and it differs most from POLAR in the connected-side reaction energy
  (−4.62 against −19.17 kJ/mol).
- **That does not make OMOL more accurate.** A lower barrier is not a better barrier. These are
  two models on one reconstructed cluster with no reference calculation; **DFT is required to
  decide which model is closer to the target surface.**

## Is the gap just geometry or path noise? {#sec-geometry}

A fair worry: OMOL and POLAR relax to slightly different structures, so the gap could reflect
which geometries were used. The check is to evaluate **both** models on **both** sets of saved
structures, with single-point energies and no relaxation.

OMOL stays **33 to 51 kJ/mol** below POLAR on every structure set tested, so the disagreement
is a **difference between the two potential-energy surfaces**, not just relaxation or path noise.
This shows the gap is not a geometry artefact. It does not explain why the models differ, and it
does not say which one is right.

## Saddle certification is not path convergence {#sec-neb}

For MACE-OMOL these are two separate facts, and only one of them is good news.

```{=html}
<div class="lanes reveal">
  <div class="lane diag">
    <span class="tag wip state">Unconverged · diagnostic only</span>
    <h4>13-image climbing-image NEB</h4>
    <div class="gauge" role="img" aria-label="NEB force 0.594 electron-volts per angstrom, about twelve times above the 0.05 target, on a logarithmic axis">
      <div class="track"><div class="fill" style="--w:88.7%"></div>
        <span class="tick" style="--x:34.9%" data-l="target 0.05"></span></div>
      <div class="legend"><span>0.01</span><span>fmax 0.594 eV/Å after 1500 steps</span><span>1</span></div>
    </div>
    <ul>
      <li>Did <strong>not</strong> converge: fmax 0.594 eV/Å against a target of 0.05.</li>
      <li>No converged reaction path or minimum-energy path is claimed.</li>
      <li>Its highest image is only a starting guess: <strong>not</strong> the transition state and <strong>not</strong> a barrier.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="lane">
    <span class="tag cert state">Converged · certified</span>
    <h4>Sella saddle search from that guess</h4>
    <div class="gauge" role="img" aria-label="Sella force 7.1 times ten to the minus four electron-volts per angstrom, below the 1 times ten to the minus three target, on a logarithmic axis">
      <div class="track"><div class="fill" style="--w:21.3%"></div>
        <span class="tick" style="--x:25.0%" data-l="target 1×10⁻³"></span></div>
      <div class="legend"><span>10⁻⁴</span><span>fmax 7.1×10⁻⁴ eV/Å in 26 steps</span><span>1</span></div>
    </div>
    <ul>
      <li>Own Hessian: exactly one imaginary mode, −1299 cm⁻¹, overlap 0.72 with the hydride transfer.</li>
      <li>±mode relaxations reach a reactant-like and a product-like minimum; Sn shell, bound water and hydride state intact on both.</li>
      <li>A different seed, Tian's POLAR saddle, converges to the <strong>same</strong> OMOL saddle (same energy, RMSD 0.001 Å).</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

The certification rule is about the **saddle only**. It requires a converged Sella search, one
imaginary mode, a hydride-transfer mode, and valid ± minima; it does not depend on how the
starting guess was found. The NEB status is reported next to it and never merged into it.

## POLAR: independently re-run through our pipeline {#sec-polar}

Tian's MACE-POLAR numbers were first recomputed from his saved raw energies. Our pipeline then
re-ran the cheap validation ladder on them:

::: {.checklist .done}
- The endpoint inputs were already POLAR-relaxed (our relaxation took 0 steps).
- Tian's saddle was already stationary (fmax 6.9×10⁻⁴ eV/Å; our Sella record is 0 steps).
- **Hessian recomputed:** one imaginary mode, −923.08 cm⁻¹, overlap 0.75 with the hydride transfer.
- **±mode connectivity recomputed:** reactant-like and product-like side minima.
- **Barriers reproduced exactly:** 112.97 (`relaxed_endpoint`) and 126.41 (`connected_side_minimum`) kJ/mol.
- **Reaction energies reproduced:** −30.02 and −19.17 kJ/mol.
- The POLAR saddle is **certified** under the same rules as OMOL's.
:::

One limit on that evidence: because the saddle was already stationary, the Sella record is
trivial, so the independent evidence is our Hessian and the ±mode connectivity. The path
behind Tian's saddle was a relaxed scan, not an NEB, and was not re-run.

## The reference you measure from matters {#sec-energy}

::: {.wide-figure}
![The POLAR reference-state example: one saddle measured from two reactant references. Solid:
the relaxed input endpoints (barrier 112.97, ΔE −30.02 kJ/mol). Dashed: the minima reached by
relaxing away from the saddle along its imaginary mode (barrier 126.41, ΔE −19.17 kJ/mol).
The reactant-side minimum R′ lies 13.44 kJ/mol below the relaxed input reactant R while its
reactive core is essentially unchanged (RMSD 0.08 Å). Energies are relative to R, in vacuum,
not free energies. Source:
`audit/tian_tt_test/tian_polar_summary.json`, recomputed from Tian's
saved total energies and reproduced by our re-run.](assets/sn_beta_energy_profile.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Energy-level diagram of the MACE-POLAR example: relaxed input reactant R at 0, reactant-side connected minimum R′ at −13.44, transition state at +112.97, product-side connected minimum P′ at −32.60 and relaxed input product P at −30.02 kJ/mol, with barrier arrows of 112.97 (from R) and 126.41 (from R′)."}
:::

This is a **scientific result**, not a loose end. Moving from the relaxed input reactant R to the
TS-connected nearby conformer R′ shifts the reported barrier by:

- **13.4 kJ/mol for POLAR** (112.97 → 126.41), and
- **18.4 kJ/mol for OMOL** (72.33 → 90.77).

```{=html}
<div class="dumb reveal" role="img" aria-label="Forward barrier measured from two reactant references. MACE-POLAR: 112.97 from the relaxed input reactant and 126.41 from the connected reactant-side minimum, a shift of 13.4 kilojoules per mole. MACE-OMOL: 72.33 and 90.77, a shift of 18.4 kilojoules per mole.">
  <div class="drow">
    <b>MACE-POLAR</b>
    <div class="dtrack"><span class="dseg" style="--a:80.7%;--b:90.3%"></span><span class="dot ep" style="--x:80.7%" data-v="112.97"></span><span class="dot cs" style="--x:90.3%" data-v="126.41"></span></div>
    <span class="dlab">+13.4<small>kJ/mol</small></span>
  </div>
  <div class="drow">
    <b>MACE-OMOL</b>
    <div class="dtrack"><span class="dseg" style="--a:51.7%;--b:64.8%"></span><span class="dot ep" style="--x:51.7%" data-v="72.33"></span><span class="dot cs" style="--x:64.8%" data-v="90.77"></span></div>
    <span class="dlab">+18.4<small>kJ/mol</small></span>
  </div>
  <div class="dscale"><span></span><span class="s"><span>0</span><span>70</span><span>140 kJ/mol</span></span><span></span></div>
  <div class="dleg"><i class="ep"></i>from <code>relaxed_endpoint</code> R <i class="cs"></i>from <code>connected_side_minimum</code> R′</div>
</div>
```

In both models the reactive core barely changes (reactive-core RMSD 0.083 Å for POLAR, 0.019 Å
for OMOL), while one backbone torsion, C1–C2–C4–O5, turns by about −70° (POLAR) or −87° (OMOL).
Both shifts are above the roughly 10 kJ/mol level we use to call a change material (an analysis
threshold, not a universal one). **Which nearby reactant structure defines the reference changes
the barrier materially**, so any comparison must say which one it uses.

R′ is a lower **local** minimum, reached by relaxing away from the saddle. It is not shown to be
the global minimum, and no conformer search has been done. No sampled structure should be read
as the global minimum.

## GFN2-xTB: a structural negative result {#sec-xtb}

**Status: structurally invalid for barrier comparison.** The reactant loses the water
(2.31 → 3.12 Å), so the xTB system is no longer the same chemistry as the MACE ones. The
product stays intact, but a barrier needs both ends. We therefore show **no xTB barrier**, did
not run a path search with it, and do not treat xTB as a reference. The failure is loss of Sn
coordination, not simply a "bad barrier".

## Which OMOL checkpoint? {#sec-checkpoint}

::: {.methodnote}
[A training-subset comparison, not model-size scaling]{.lbl}
The MACE-OMOL release provides no smaller model: both checkpoints are the same extra-large
architecture. The only second checkpoint, trained on a 4M subset of the data, was run through a
cheap ladder (relaxation, Sella seeded from the 1024 saddle, Hessian, ±mode connectivity). Barriers
move by **+0.86** (`relaxed_endpoint`) and **−0.61** kJ/mol (`connected_side_minimum`); the
relaxed-endpoint ΔE shifts by about **6.0** kJ/mol (−27.22 → −21.20) for a reason we have not
isolated. This is a small check, not a scaling law, and its saddle was seeded from the 1024
saddle, so it is not an independent path search. Do not over-interpret it.
:::

## What is and is not established {#sec-reconstructed}

[Directly demonstrated]{.tag .demo} — from the benchmark run and its saved outputs:

- **Two certified saddles.** MACE-OMOL-1024 and MACE-POLAR each give a verified first-order
  saddle, with valid reactant-like and product-like ± minima, on this reconstructed cluster.
- **Tian's POLAR numbers are reproduced** by our Hessian and connectivity re-run.
- **The two models disagree on energetics:** forward barriers differ by 40.6 / 35.6 kJ/mol
  (depending on reference state), and the gap persists at identical saved geometries.
- **The reported barrier depends on the reference conformer:** by 13.4 kJ/mol (POLAR) and
  18.4 kJ/mol (OMOL).
- **GFN2-xTB loses the Sn-bound water** in the reactant relaxation.
- **OMOL's 13-image CI-NEB did not converge** (fmax 0.594 against a target of 0.05 eV/Å).

[Supported interpretation]{.tag .interp} The two models describe the same chemical event (one
hydride-transfer saddle with a hydride-dominated imaginary mode) but through different surfaces.
The 1024 and 4M OMOL checkpoints agree to within about 1 kJ/mol on the barrier.

[Not demonstrated]{.tag .open} These are not established:

- **accuracy against DFT**, or which model is closer to it: no reference calculation exists yet
- a **converged reaction path** for OMOL
- that R′, or any sampled conformer, is the **lowest** conformer
- that the reconstructed cluster is the **original literature geometry**, or that the charge and
  spin (0 / singlet) are the right ones
- any solvent effect, or any free-energy or experimental comparison.

## Does the reconstructed chemistry look right? {#sec-structure}

::: {.wide-figure}
![Orthogonal views of the reactant, transition state and product in a common Sn-centred
frame: origin at Sn, x toward the C1/C2 midpoint, z normal to the O1–Sn–O2 plane. Distances
in Å, measured from the coordinates. A qualitative check only, not a pass/fail criterion.
Same frame as the committed audit image
`sweep/sn_beta_hydride/audit/tian_tt_test/structure_views.png`; generated by
`site/build_sn_beta_figures.py`.](assets/sn_beta_structure_views.png){width="100%" fig-alt="Three-by-three grid of orthogonal projections of reactant, transition state and product, with the Sn centre and the transferring hydride H* highlighted."}
:::

::: {.observations}
- Hydride on **C2** in the reactant (C2–H\* 1.10 Å, C1–H\* 2.11 Å)
- **Shared** between C2 and C1 at the transition state (1.31 / 1.35 Å)
- Hydride on **C1** in the product (2.12 / 1.10 Å)
- At Sn, O1 and O2 swap roles as intended: Sn–O1 2.34 → 1.99 Å, Sn–O2 2.04 → 2.47 Å
- Six O lie within 2.8 Å of Sn in both endpoints. In the product Sn–O2 (2.47 Å) is just beyond a
  2.46 Å bond criterion, so five O are within it: a coordination change, not a neutral swap
- Reconstructed structures: hand-built and relaxed with MACE-POLAR-1-S, **not** original
  CPMD coordinates
:::

## Background and provenance {#sec-question}

**Reference.** S. H. Mushrif, J. J. Varghese, C. B. Krishnamurthy, *Solvation dynamics
and energetics of intramolecular hydride transfer reactions in biomass conversion*,
Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. **17**, 4961–4969 (2015),
DOI [10.1039/C4CP05063K](https://doi.org/10.1039/C4CP05063K).

The immediate experiment is narrower than the original study: whether these models give
a physically meaningful transition pathway between known initial and final states,
initially *without* reproducing the full explicit-solvent metadynamics.

**The reconstructed model.** Tian built a 42-atom vacuum model by hand: open-chain
glucose bound to a SiH₃-capped Sn site, C₆H₂₂O₁₀Si₃Sn, interpreting the literature
drawing. He relaxed it with MACE-POLAR-1-S and ran a relaxed scan, a Sella saddle
search and a Hessian. These are **not** the paper's coordinates. The neutral singlet
charge state is an **inferred** model choice, not literature-confirmed.

Sources:
[`audit/omol_benchmark/`](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/ml-accelerated-metadynamics/tree/main/sweep/sn_beta_hydride/audit/omol_benchmark)
(curated benchmark results),
[`OMOL_BENCHMARK_REPORT.md`](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/ml-accelerated-metadynamics/blob/main/sweep/sn_beta_hydride/OMOL_BENCHMARK_REPORT.md),
[`audit/tian_tt_test/`](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/ml-accelerated-metadynamics/tree/main/sweep/sn_beta_hydride/audit/tian_tt_test)
(`tian_polar_summary.json`, `input_validation.json`, `structure_views.png`) and
[`input/tian_tt_test/provenance.json`](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/ml-accelerated-metadynamics/tree/main/sweep/sn_beta_hydride/input/tian_tt_test).

### Why new foundation models {#sec-why}

MACE-OFF23, used for the Diels–Alder benchmark, was trained on organic chemistry and
has no tin. MACE-OMOL-0 and MACE-POLAR-1 cover elements up to Z = 83, Sn included, and
both take the system's total charge and spin multiplicity as inputs. MACE-POLAR adds
long-range electrostatics. This is the first test of the project's pipeline on a
catalytic, metal-containing system.

### Pipeline and checks {#sec-infrastructure}

[Exercised on the real cluster]{.tag .demo} by this benchmark:

::: {.checklist .done}
- Strict structure validation that refuses to start a calculation on invalid input
- Endpoint relaxation, CI-NEB, Sella saddle refinement, mass-weighted Hessian
  ([standard](methods.qmd#sec-ts)) and ±imaginary-mode connectivity
- Barriers and reaction energies always reported against a named reference state — the
  relaxed input endpoints, or the minima connected to the saddle
- Total charge and multiplicity always set explicitly; the models otherwise default silently
  to a neutral singlet
- GFN2-xTB as a third method under the same protocol (used here as a structural check)
:::

Added with the benchmark, after review:

::: {.checklist .done}
- A saddle is certified only with a **converged Sella search** on record, one imaginary mode,
  a hydride-transfer mode, and valid ± minima
- Each ± side minimum must keep its Sn shell, bound water, heavy-atom bonds and hydride state
  relative to the input structure; an invalid side gives no reference energy
- NEB status is reported separately from the saddle label, so an unconverged NEB can never be
  mistaken for a converged path
:::

[Built, tested on synthetic fixtures only]{.tag .wip} Gaussian-log ingestion, DFT-against-MACE
energy and force metrics, and a sparse-DFT-label experiment framework. They have never been run on
real Gaussian output. A metadynamics readiness checklist exists; **no MACE metadynamics has been
launched**.

### Blocked on authoritative information {#sec-blockers}

[Work in progress]{.tag .wip} The production configuration for **authoritative**
structures still stops before loading a model, by design, until these are supplied:

::: {.checklist .blocked}
- Authoritative reactant coordinates
- Authoritative product coordinates
- Total charge
- Spin multiplicity
- Atom mapping (which atoms are C1, C2, the transferring hydride, Sn, and the
  coordinating oxygens)
- The original CPMD collective-variable parameters d₀, p, q
- Fixed / capped-atom policy for the cluster model
- The intended solvent / cluster representation for this experiment
:::

### What the literature does and does not establish {#sec-literature}

The paper itself is closed access and has not been read in full; the points below come
from its abstract and from a thesis that reproduces its Fig. 1 (M. A. Y. Ali, MSc thesis,
University of Alberta, 2025). Nothing here has been checked against the paper's full
text.

- [Literature]{.tag .lit} **Protocols.** The paper uses CPMD-metadynamics with explicit water
  or methanol, a CPMD-metadynamics run without solvent, and implicit-solvent DFT
  (abstract). The thesis's own dataset is a 20,000-timestep **gas-phase** run; whether it
  is the paper's solvent-free run is not established.
- [Literature, as drawn]{.tag .lit} **Model.** The thesis figure adapted from the paper draws the
  site as a SiH₃-capped Sn cluster, Sn(–O–SiH₃)₃, with open-chain glucose bound through
  its C1 and C2 oxygens and the water formed at the site remaining on Sn.
- [Literature, secondary]{.tag .lit} **Collective variables.** CV1 is the coordination
  number of C1 with the two hydrogens H1 and H2; CV2 is the coordination number of C2
  with the same two hydrogens, using CPMD's rational coordination function.
- [Unknown]{.tag .open} **CV parameters d₀, p, q.** The project's code computes these CVs
  with **placeholder** parameters that are explicitly flagged as unconfirmed, and refuses
  to compare against the reference basin values until the originals are supplied.
- [Unknown]{.tag .open} **Charge and multiplicity** — not stated in either source.

::: {.methodnote}
[Not a reference value]{.lbl}
The "≈82 kJ/mol barrier" sometimes quoted for this reaction comes from data tips on the
thesis's **gas-phase metadynamics free-energy plot**, not from a verified published value.
It is a free-energy difference from a biased-sampling run; an endpoint-to-endpoint NEB or
Sella calculation gives a potential-energy barrier, and the two are not directly
comparable. It is not used here as ground truth.
:::

The code and its tests are in
[`sweep/sn_beta_hydride/`](https://github.com/tiangroup-uofa/ml-accelerated-metadynamics/tree/main/sweep/sn_beta_hydride),
with the full literature audit in its README.
